title: more frustrating than enjoyable
content:
I was a paid customer but have left the service. I really loved the idea and thought the pricing was fair, and my initial reaction overall was positive. But lately I’ve been opening the app less and less because too often I end up with audio I dislike that doesn’t adapt to my feedback, or audio that sounds “buggy,” like the AI has stopped responding. I’ve tried to use the Like/Dislike buttons constructively to help personalize the service, but I don’t hear it helping, and it’s starting to feel like I’m interacting with static tracks that don’t actually have any dynamic AI element. 

Example 1: On one song, a distracting human voice started popping up to utter one phrase over and over. I gave the app a Dislike and waited for it to change, but it didn’t. I Disliked it again — nothing. I hit the refresh button to see if that would reset some parameters and change things up, but got the voice again. I finally gave up.

Example 2: Another song started off fine and I was really digging it, but then slowly all but one element of the song just… went away… leaving behind only a synthesized “waves crashing” sound effect over a bed of nothingness. I tapped Dislike. No change, still just waves crashing. I tapped Dislike over 20 times. Still just waves. I hit the refresh button, and then the track stopped playing entirely. I restarted the app and went back to that song and got the exact same experience, where after maybe 30 seconds all the elements faded out to leave just waves crashing.

title: I’m picky about my LoFi, but...
content:
I don’t usually review but I was weirdly impressed with this and I saw it wasn’t getting a lot of downloads for whatever reason. 

So, I’m picky about my Lo-Fi, and even more picky about my ambient study music. It has to be a certain level of detailed musically but also uninteresting enough that it doesn’t distract me. 

Endel is good app for this, but I’ve recently switched to this one. I didn’t think I could be converted, but, I have to say, I study better, read with less distraction, and when I play it when I’m working, I find that I complete tedious tasks with an overall more positive and focused attitude. 

The ability to flatten out the musical detail (for better focus) with the touch of one button was a really smart feature to add to this. 

I’m really liking the fact that there is an infinite amount of new music (generated by AI, which you can “train” with a like/dislike option), but at the same time, there’s an extremely limited amount of decisions you have to make about it... so there’s no analysis paralysis when it comes to what to listen to. 

For that reason, it’s kind of perfect for people who get lost when there are too many options, but get bored when there is too much repetition.

I’m sure someone else has encountered this, too...so hopefully there will soon be a fix for this.  Otherwise, this app is great!

New updated version (December 23, 2020).  Nope!!!  It was better before this new updated version.  They say they’ve added new, more music...yeah, if you want to buy/pay for it!  Many of the channels that were free before this update you now have to buy/pay for!  I see the beginning of the end here with an app that was one of my favorites.  What else can I say?  This just comes across as a pure greedy move by the developers.  If they had added new music channels as pay options, cool.  But to take away ones that were free all along and now charge you for them...get lost!  My original 4 stars is down to 2 stars (unless Mubert realizes this and changes it back).

title: Shady Business Practices
content:
It’s bad enough this is a subscription service but the “free trial” they offer is super sketchy. If you use the free trial option, once the trial period ends you do not have an option of which billing option you can choose, they force you into the 12 month paid in advance option that’s it; which is utterly ridiculous. The shadiest most shameful part in my eyes is the fact that if you didn’t enjoy the service enough to pay the high 12 month in advance amount and decide to cancel, you don’t have up until the final second of the “trial period” like you do with literally every other subscription service I’ve ever seen, you actually have to cancel no later than 24 hours before the final second of the trial period. 

So not only are you not getting the full trial period they claim, this company is Obviously doing it to try and catch people who either didn’t see the note about the 24 hours or didn’t fully understand it because it doesn’t make much sense so they can force that full 12 month advance payment even from people who have no interest whatsoever in paying upfront for 12 months. 

That is extremely dishonest and bad bad business. If your product can’t speak for itself and do what it’s supposed to do while getting people excited enough about it in the process to knowingly pay the 12 month payment then the product shouldn’t be priced this high and there should be the option to go from the trial to the 30 day billing option, and maybe more effort should be put into the app design/capabilities so that more people will want you pay for it. I will never pay for this app or any others that do shady business like this. 

Beware everyone, watch the billing on this one...

title: Not True AI
content: If you sign up for Mubert Pro online, then you get a glimpse into how Mubert music is made. Despite slick ultra modern graphic design, it is actually very primitive. Mubert takes prerecorded samples and arranges them randomly. It does not actually randomly generate new music (no new melodies, harmonies, or rhythms). It takes prerecorded melodies, harmonies, and rhythms and arranges them in random orders. Mubert is repetitive club muzak. I give it two stars instead of one because Mubert’s excellent  graphic design deserves a star.

Comically bad for a $7/month subscription.  Canceled subscription and recommend others avoid until they actually purchase an email account or other method for support that a human actually pays attention to.

title: Passes the Turing Hearing Test (if one existed)
content:
For what is being offered the experience is great. Dynamic noises and never any sloppy transitions through the music. I would be interested in the ability for Mubert to offer a more personalized experience for the user. This would require the model to more robust but I think would pay dividends along the line. For a more simple approach you could offer a Thumbs Up/Down to gain a users sentiment of the current track to offer more personalization. Future features like user uploaded .wav files of favorite music to add further personalization to the model would be neat. 

This type of technology excites me so I just think of all the different types of applications that could be added in. This is among the first applications in a soon to come industry that has offered a great service. Keep it up!
